contribution.position: My position is unchanged: reliability evidence is still incomplete. The test report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) and the perf report (p99 within budget at peak) are healthy, but neither exercises retry or failure-amplification behavior. The incident log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both traced to retry storms, and nothing provided shows this change under retry-storm or fault-injection conditions. On recovery, the ops claim of a clean restore test cites artifact:restore-test-2026-08, which is not among the available artifacts and is not anchored. It also conflicts with the runbook, which says nightly backups have never had a restore tested. Until that restore result is produced and checked against the runbook, I treat the recovery path as unproven. Two small, bounded items would close this: (1) a retry-storm or fault-injection result for this change, and (2) a documented, successful restore drill from the nightly backup, with the runbook updated to match.
